text:
# Abstract

GEO series GSE309890 was evaluated to determine whether raw reads are available and whether they are suitable for sequence assembly. The GEO record describes six *Escherichia coli* K-12 MG1655 samples and links the series to BioProject PRJNA1363958. Querying that project in NCBI SRA and ENA identified six public runs, all generated as paired-end, 300-base-per-spot Illumina HiSeq 4000 RNA-seq libraries. Together they contain 69,110,351 read pairs, corresponding to 138,220,702 reads and 20,733,105,300 sequenced bases. ENA provides 12 directly downloadable FASTQ files totaling 6,818,365,912 compressed bytes, approximately 6.82 GB. Therefore, the raw reads can be obtained. However, these are transcriptomic cDNA reads rather than genomic DNA reads. They are appropriate for reference-based expression analysis and potentially exploratory transcript assembly, but not for a reliable de novo assembly of the complete bacterial genome: unexpressed and weakly expressed regions will have absent or uneven coverage. The BRC workflow catalog returned one assembly-category workflow, but it performs polishing with long reads and does not accept these paired-end RNA-seq reads as an assembly input. For this dataset, reference-based RNA-seq analysis against MG1655 assembly GCF_000005845.2 is the supported route; genomic assembly would require genomic WGS or long-read data.

# I. Introduction

**Background.** GSE309890 is an expression-profiling series containing six RNA-seq samples from *Escherichia coli* strain K-12 substrain MG1655. The experiment compares three controls with three 40-day adaptive-evolution samples. GEO links the series to BioProject PRJNA1363958.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. GEO reports no linked PubMed record.

**Knowledge Gap.** The GEO page exposes one processed FPKM matrix, but the availability, format, volume, and assembly suitability of the underlying raw reads required examination of the linked sequencing archive.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The objective was to determine whether raw reads can be downloaded and whether an assembly workflow can appropriately process them. The expectation was that raw reads would be available through the linked SRA project, but their suitability would depend on library strategy and layout.

# II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** The GEO series was first retrieved to identify samples and linked accessions. The linked BioProject was then searched in SRA for run-level metadata. ENA was queried for direct paired FASTQ links. BRC organism, assembly, and workflow catalogs were searched to evaluate reference availability and workflow compatibility.

**Materials.**

- NCBI GEO, accessed with `geo_series`.
- NCBI SRA, accessed with `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project`.
- ENA, accessed with `brc_ena_study`.
- BRC organism and assembly catalogs, accessed with `search_organisms` and `get_assemblies`.
- BRC/IWC workflow catalog, accessed with `list_workflow_categories` and `get_workflows_in_category`.

**Procedures.**

1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true)`.
2. `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project(accession="PRJNA1363958", max_results=100, start=0)`.
3. In parallel:
   - `search_organisms(query="Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655", limit=10)`.
   - `list_workflow_categories()`.
4. Because the strain-specific organism query returned no direct organism record, the broader species and relevant workflow categories were queried:
   - `search_organisms(query="Escherichia coli", limit=10)`.
   - `get_workflows_in_category(category="ASSEMBLY")`.
   - `get_workflows_in_category(category="TRANSCRIPTOMICS")`.
5. `get_assemblies(taxonomy_id="562")`.
6. `brc_ena_study(study_accession="PRJNA1363958")` to retrieve direct FASTQ download URLs.

**Statistical Analysis.** Runs were deduplicated by SRA run accession. Run count was taken from the six distinct SRR accessions. Total read pairs were calculated by summing the SRA/ENA spot or read-count fields; all runs were paired and had mates for every spot. Total individual reads were calculated as twice the number of pairs. Total bases and compressed FASTQ bytes were summed across all runs and files. Percentages use six runs as the denominator.

# III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Raw sequencing data associated with GSE309890**

| Sample | Condition | Run | Read pairs | Bases | Compressed FASTQ | Downloads |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GSM9284457 | Control, replicate 1 | SRR36018645 | 11,621,726 | 3,486,517,800 | 1,099,095,024 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_2.fastq.gz) |
| GSM9284458 | Control, replicate 2 | SRR36018644 | 10,415,434 | 3,124,630,200 | 990,814,552 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_2.fastq.gz) |
| GSM9284459 | Control, replicate 3 | SRR36018643 | 11,720,219 | 3,516,065,700 | 1,114,579,166 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_2.fastq.gz) |
| GSM9284460 | Adaptive evolution, day 40, replicate 1 | SRR36018642 | 11,992,461 | 3,597,738,300 | 1,250,892,876 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_2.fastq.gz) |
| GSM9284461 | Adaptive evolution, day 40, replicate 2 | SRR36018641 | 11,997,182 | 3,599,154,600 | 1,213,834,497 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_2.fastq.gz) |
| GSM9284462 | Adaptive evolution, day 40, replicate 3 | SRR36018640 | 11,363,329 | 3,408,998,700 | 1,149,149,797 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_2.fastq.gz) |
| **Total** | 3 control + 3 evolved | **6 runs** | **69,110,351** | **20,733,105,300** | **6,818,365,912 bytes** | **12 FASTQ files** |

**Table 2. Suitability for available analysis routes**

| Analysis route | Suitability | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Reference-based RNA-seq analysis | Suitable | All 6/6 runs are paired-end RNA-seq; the BRC catalog contains a paired-end RNA-seq workflow. |
| De novo transcript assembly | Technically possible | Reads represent expressed RNA; resulting contigs would represent transcripts or expressed regions, not the complete genome. |
| De novo genome assembly | Not recommended | All 6/6 libraries are transcriptomic cDNA rather than genomic DNA, producing expression-dependent and incomplete genome coverage. |
| BRC assembly-category workflow | Not compatible as a primary assembler | The only returned workflow was “Assembly polishing with long reads,” requiring an existing assembly FASTA and long reads. |
| Reference genome | Available | MG1655 complete reference assembly GCF_000005845.2, length 4,641,652 bases, one chromosome, haploid. |

**Findings.**

- Raw paired FASTQ files are publicly downloadable for all six samples.
- All six runs are RNA-seq, cDNA, transcriptomic, paired-end Illumina HiSeq 4000 libraries.
- The dataset contains 69,110,351 read pairs, or 138,220,702 individual reads.
- The direct compressed FASTQ download is approximately 6.82 GB.
- GEO itself provides only the processed file `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz`; the raw data are stored in SRA/ENA.
- The paired-end BRC RNA-seq workflow matches the reported layout and strategy.
- The assembly workflow returned by the catalog is a long-read polishing workflow, not a short-read de novo assembler.

# IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** Yes, the raw reads can be downloaded. No, they should not be used to infer a complete de novo MG1655 genome assembly. RNA-seq samples only molecules that were transcribed under the experimental conditions, and coverage varies with expression. Consequently, genomic regions with no detectable transcription may be absent, while highly expressed genes may be overrepresented.

If “assembly” means transcript reconstruction, a de novo transcript assembler can be applied separately to each condition or to pooled reads. Its output should be described as a transcriptome or expressed-sequence assembly, not a genome assembly. For this bacterial experiment, reference alignment and gene-level quantification are generally more directly matched to the study design.

The most appropriate available workflow is the paired-end RNA-seq workflow, using reference assembly GCF_000005845.2 and its gene model. Each biological replicate should remain separate rather than pooling all reads before expression analysis.

**Context.** The series was explicitly classified as “Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing.” Its processed supplementary file contains FPKM values, while the linked SRA/ENA records provide raw paired FASTQ data. The reference assembly belongs to the same reported MG1655 strain.

**Limitations.** Library strandedness was not reported in the retrieved run metadata. Insert-size fields were zero and therefore did not provide a usable fragment-size estimate. The retrieved workflow catalog contained no general paired-end short-read genome assembler and no dedicated bacterial de novo transcript-assembly workflow. RNA-seq data cannot establish complete genome sequence, genome-wide structural variation, or absence of mutations in regions lacking adequate transcript coverage. RNA-derived variant calls can also be affected by expression level and mapping artifacts.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** Download the 12 ENA FASTQ files and use a paired-end, reference-based RNA-seq pipeline against GCF_000005845.2. Run a de novo transcript assembly only if transcript discovery is the objective. To reconstruct the evolved bacterial genomes or characterize fixed `rpoBC` and `gyrAB` mutations comprehensively, the next query should search for matched WGS or long-read libraries from the same evolved isolates.

summary.question: I have a GEO series, GSE309890. Can I get the raw reads and run an assembly on them?
summary.answer:
# Abstract

GEO series GSE309890 was evaluated to determine whether raw reads are available and whether they are suitable for sequence assembly. The GEO record describes six *Escherichia coli* K-12 MG1655 samples and links the series to BioProject PRJNA1363958. Querying that project in NCBI SRA and ENA identified six public runs, all generated as paired-end, 300-base-per-spot Illumina HiSeq 4000 RNA-seq libraries. Together they contain 69,110,351 read pairs, corresponding to 138,220,702 reads and 20,733,105,300 sequenced bases. ENA provides 12 directly downloadable FASTQ files totaling 6,818,365,912 compressed bytes, approximately 6.82 GB. Therefore, the raw reads can be obtained. However, these are transcriptomic cDNA reads rather than genomic DNA reads. They are appropriate for reference-based expression analysis and potentially exploratory transcript assembly, but not for a reliable de novo assembly of the complete bacterial genome: unexpressed and weakly expressed regions will have absent or uneven coverage. The BRC workflow catalog returned one assembly-category workflow, but it performs polishing with long reads and does not accept these paired-end RNA-seq reads as an assembly input. For this dataset, reference-based RNA-seq analysis against MG1655 assembly GCF_000005845.2 is the supported route; genomic assembly would require genomic WGS or long-read data.

# I. Introduction

**Background.** GSE309890 is an expression-profiling series containing six RNA-seq samples from *Escherichia coli* strain K-12 substrain MG1655. The experiment compares three controls with three 40-day adaptive-evolution samples. GEO links the series to BioProject PRJNA1363958.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. GEO reports no linked PubMed record.

**Knowledge Gap.** The GEO page exposes one processed FPKM matrix, but the availability, format, volume, and assembly suitability of the underlying raw reads required examination of the linked sequencing archive.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The objective was to determine whether raw reads can be downloaded and whether an assembly workflow can appropriately process them. The expectation was that raw reads would be available through the linked SRA project, but their suitability would depend on library strategy and layout.

# II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** The GEO series was first retrieved to identify samples and linked accessions. The linked BioProject was then searched in SRA for run-level metadata. ENA was queried for direct paired FASTQ links. BRC organism, assembly, and workflow catalogs were searched to evaluate reference availability and workflow compatibility.

**Materials.**

- NCBI GEO, accessed with `geo_series`.
- NCBI SRA, accessed with `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project`.
- ENA, accessed with `brc_ena_study`.
- BRC organism and assembly catalogs, accessed with `search_organisms` and `get_assemblies`.
- BRC/IWC workflow catalog, accessed with `list_workflow_categories` and `get_workflows_in_category`.

**Procedures.**

1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true)`.
2. `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project(accession="PRJNA1363958", max_results=100, start=0)`.
3. In parallel:
   - `search_organisms(query="Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655", limit=10)`.
   - `list_workflow_categories()`.
4. Because the strain-specific organism query returned no direct organism record, the broader species and relevant workflow categories were queried:
   - `search_organisms(query="Escherichia coli", limit=10)`.
   - `get_workflows_in_category(category="ASSEMBLY")`.
   - `get_workflows_in_category(category="TRANSCRIPTOMICS")`.
5. `get_assemblies(taxonomy_id="562")`.
6. `brc_ena_study(study_accession="PRJNA1363958")` to retrieve direct FASTQ download URLs.

**Statistical Analysis.** Runs were deduplicated by SRA run accession. Run count was taken from the six distinct SRR accessions. Total read pairs were calculated by summing the SRA/ENA spot or read-count fields; all runs were paired and had mates for every spot. Total individual reads were calculated as twice the number of pairs. Total bases and compressed FASTQ bytes were summed across all runs and files. Percentages use six runs as the denominator.

# III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Raw sequencing data associated with GSE309890**

| Sample | Condition | Run | Read pairs | Bases | Compressed FASTQ | Downloads |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GSM9284457 | Control, replicate 1 | SRR36018645 | 11,621,726 | 3,486,517,800 | 1,099,095,024 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_2.fastq.gz) |
| GSM9284458 | Control, replicate 2 | SRR36018644 | 10,415,434 | 3,124,630,200 | 990,814,552 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_2.fastq.gz) |
| GSM9284459 | Control, replicate 3 | SRR36018643 | 11,720,219 | 3,516,065,700 | 1,114,579,166 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_2.fastq.gz) |
| GSM9284460 | Adaptive evolution, day 40, replicate 1 | SRR36018642 | 11,992,461 | 3,597,738,300 | 1,250,892,876 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_2.fastq.gz) |
| GSM9284461 | Adaptive evolution, day 40, replicate 2 | SRR36018641 | 11,997,182 | 3,599,154,600 | 1,213,834,497 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_2.fastq.gz) |
| GSM9284462 | Adaptive evolution, day 40, replicate 3 | SRR36018640 | 11,363,329 | 3,408,998,700 | 1,149,149,797 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_1.fastq.gz), [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_2.fastq.gz) |
| **Total** | 3 control + 3 evolved | **6 runs** | **69,110,351** | **20,733,105,300** | **6,818,365,912 bytes** | **12 FASTQ files** |

**Table 2. Suitability for available analysis routes**

| Analysis route | Suitability | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Reference-based RNA-seq analysis | Suitable | All 6/6 runs are paired-end RNA-seq; the BRC catalog contains a paired-end RNA-seq workflow. |
| De novo transcript assembly | Technically possible | Reads represent expressed RNA; resulting contigs would represent transcripts or expressed regions, not the complete genome. |
| De novo genome assembly | Not recommended | All 6/6 libraries are transcriptomic cDNA rather than genomic DNA, producing expression-dependent and incomplete genome coverage. |
| BRC assembly-category workflow | Not compatible as a primary assembler | The only returned workflow was “Assembly polishing with long reads,” requiring an existing assembly FASTA and long reads. |
| Reference genome | Available | MG1655 complete reference assembly GCF_000005845.2, length 4,641,652 bases, one chromosome, haploid. |

**Findings.**

- Raw paired FASTQ files are publicly downloadable for all six samples.
- All six runs are RNA-seq, cDNA, transcriptomic, paired-end Illumina HiSeq 4000 libraries.
- The dataset contains 69,110,351 read pairs, or 138,220,702 individual reads.
- The direct compressed FASTQ download is approximately 6.82 GB.
- GEO itself provides only the processed file `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz`; the raw data are stored in SRA/ENA.
- The paired-end BRC RNA-seq workflow matches the reported layout and strategy.
- The assembly workflow returned by the catalog is a long-read polishing workflow, not a short-read de novo assembler.

# IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** Yes, the raw reads can be downloaded. No, they should not be used to infer a complete de novo MG1655 genome assembly. RNA-seq samples only molecules that were transcribed under the experimental conditions, and coverage varies with expression. Consequently, genomic regions with no detectable transcription may be absent, while highly expressed genes may be overrepresented.

If “assembly” means transcript reconstruction, a de novo transcript assembler can be applied separately to each condition or to pooled reads. Its output should be described as a transcriptome or expressed-sequence assembly, not a genome assembly. For this bacterial experiment, reference alignment and gene-level quantification are generally more directly matched to the study design.

The most appropriate available workflow is the paired-end RNA-seq workflow, using reference assembly GCF_000005845.2 and its gene model. Each biological replicate should remain separate rather than pooling all reads before expression analysis.

**Context.** The series was explicitly classified as “Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing.” Its processed supplementary file contains FPKM values, while the linked SRA/ENA records provide raw paired FASTQ data. The reference assembly belongs to the same reported MG1655 strain.

**Limitations.** Library strandedness was not reported in the retrieved run metadata. Insert-size fields were zero and therefore did not provide a usable fragment-size estimate. The retrieved workflow catalog contained no general paired-end short-read genome assembler and no dedicated bacterial de novo transcript-assembly workflow. RNA-seq data cannot establish complete genome sequence, genome-wide structural variation, or absence of mutations in regions lacking adequate transcript coverage. RNA-derived variant calls can also be affected by expression level and mapping artifacts.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** Download the 12 ENA FASTQ files and use a paired-end, reference-based RNA-seq pipeline against GCF_000005845.2. Run a de novo transcript assembly only if transcript discovery is the objective. To reconstruct the evolved bacterial genomes or characterize fixed `rpoBC` and `gyrAB` mutations comprehensively, the next query should search for matched WGS or long-read libraries from the same evolved isolates.
